title: Spreading a prescribed stable valuation model to a quasi-alteration
statement: Let $T$ be an integral scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $L$ be a separable closure of $k(T)$, and let $x\in RZ_L(T)$ correspond to $V$ as in [lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement]. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth generic curve and etale generic marking. Suppose a stable $\eta$-modification of $(X,D)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}V$ has been specified. Then there exists an $L$-quasi-model $U\to T$, a lift $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U$, and a stable $\eta$-modification $(Y,E)\to(X,D)\times_T U$ over the integral scheme $U$ whose pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}V$ is isomorphic to the specified modification; moreover there is a dense open $U^\circ\subseteq U$ such that both the curve map and the marking map are isomorphisms over the preimages of $U^\circ$, which contain the generic fibres. The open $RZ_L(U)$ contains $x$. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Finite type for scheme morphisms has the meaning of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2, §3.1 and Remark 3.1.1(ii), Lemma 5.1(ii) (constructibility of stable fibres), and the second paragraph of proof of Theorem 1.5, pp. 34--36. This is the approximation/constructibility step, without any assertion of global existence.

proof.text: By the definition in the statement, the specified stable $\eta$-modification consists of a multipointed $\operatorname{Spec}V$-curve $(Y_V,E_V)$ (semistable, in particular flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimensions $1$ and $0$ with $E_V\hookrightarrow Y_V$ a closed immersion) and a compatible pair of proper maps $f_X:Y_V\to X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}V$, $f_D:E_V\to D\times_T\operatorname{Spec}V$ which are isomorphisms on the fibres over $\operatorname{Spec}L$, the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}V$. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-trf-stable-modification-finite-presentation-spread] for $T$, $L$, $x$ and $(X,D)$. It gives an $L$-quasi-model $U_0\to T$, a factorization $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U_0\to T$, a multipointed $U_0$-curve $(Y_0,E_0)$ with a compatible proper pair $g=(g_X,g_D)$ to $(X,D)\times_TU_0$ which is an isomorphism on the generic fibre, and an identification of the pullback of $g$ to $\operatorname{Spec}V$ with $(f_X,f_D)$.

source.place: §3.1 and Remark 3.1.1(ii), and the second paragraph of the proof of Theorem 1.5, pp. 34--36.

proof.text: $U_0$ is integral and separated of finite type over $T$, hence of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, and its function field lies between $k(T)$ and $L$, so is algebraic over $k(T)$; thus $L$ is a separable closure of $k(U_0)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U_0$ is a point of $RZ_L(U_0)$ (elementary). Since $U_0\to T$ sends the generic point to the generic point, the first clause of [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change] shows that $(X,D)\times_TU_0$ is a multipointed $U_0$-curve with smooth generic curve and etale generic marking. Because $((X,D)\times_TU_0)\times_{U_0}\operatorname{Spec}V=(X,D)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}V$, Step 1 says that the pullback of $g$ to $\operatorname{Spec}V$ is the specified stable $\eta$-modification. Apply [lem-trf-stable-modification-stability-locus] to $U_0$, $L$, $V$, $(X,D)\times_TU_0$ and $g$: it gives an $L$-quasi-model $U\to U_0$ with a factorization $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U\to U_0$ such that $(Y,E):=(Y_0,E_0)\times_{U_0}U\to(X,D)\times_TU$ is a stable $\eta$-modification over $U$, and a dense open $U^\circ\subseteq U$ containing the generic point over whose preimages both maps are isomorphisms. The composite $U\to U_0\to T$ is separated of finite type (composites of such) and $U$ is integral with $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U\to T$, so $U$ is an $L$-quasi-model of $T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U$ lifts the given $\operatorname{Spec}V\to T$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), Remark 3.1.1(ii), and the second paragraph of the proof of Theorem 1.5, pp. 34--36.

proof.text: The pullback of $(Y,E)\to(X,D)\times_TU$ along $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U$ is $(Y_0,E_0)\times_{U_0}\operatorname{Spec}V\to(X,D)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}V$ by transitivity of fibre products, since $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U\to U_0$ is the factorization of Step 1. The isomorphisms of [lem-trf-stable-modification-finite-presentation-spread] identify it, together with the closed immersion of the marking and both pair maps, with the specified stable modification $(f_X,f_D)$. This is a rearrangement of the cited identifications.

$U$ is an integral scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and $L$ is a separable closure of $k(U)$, so by the description of points in [lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement] the factorization $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U$ is a point of $RZ_L(U)$; its image under the open injection $RZ_L(U)\hookrightarrow RZ_L(T)$ of the same statement is the composite $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U\to T$, which is $x$. Hence $x\in RZ_L(U)$. Since $U^\circ$ contains the generic point of $U$, its preimages contain the generic fibres of $(X,D)\times_TU$ and of $(Y,E)$. With Steps 2 and 3 this is every assertion of the item; no global stable-modification existence theorem is used.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2 and the second paragraph of the proof of Theorem 1.5, pp. 34--36.

Source: the Temkin PDF (arXiv 0707.3953v3) is not in literature/, so Temkin Lemma 3.2.2, Lemma 5.1(ii), Remark 3.1.1(ii) and the Thm 1.5 proof could not be read. Instead both new statements were checked from first principles. Spread node: V is the filtered union of finitely generated subalgebras A_i of an affine chart, each Spec A_i is an L-quasi-model, and the fraction fields of the A_i exhaust L; standard finite-presentation limit arguments then descend the curves, the closed immersion, properness, flatness, pure fibre dimension and the generic isomorphism. Stability node: the stable locus is a constructible set of fibre conditions containing the image of Spec V; a limit argument over the RZ models gives a quasi-model neighbourhood; the generic isomorphism spreads to a dense open; an open containing the generic fibre of a flat curve is schematically dense. Small cases tested: empty marking, trivial valuation, a point base, a pair that is already an isomorphism. Faults repaired: (1) B2/B3/B7 in lem-trf-stable-modification-finite-presentation-spread: the closed-immersion hypothesis E_V into Y_V was missing, 'multipointed pair' was undefined, the generic isomorphism over U_0 was not stated, and meanings were deferred to the item. The statement was rewritten self-contained and stmt_deps corrected. (2) B2/B3 in lem-trf-stable-modification-stability-locus: L, V, the map Spec V to U_0 and the valuation point were not introduced, and stable eta-modification was defined only by citing lemma nodes. The definitions are now written inline and uniqueness-normal was dropped from stmt_deps. (3) C4/E1 in the item: step 2 applied the stability node without checking its smooth-generic-curve and etale-marking hypothesis, which now comes from the first clause of semistable-marked-base-change. Step 3 was vague and is now an elementary transitivity of fibre products. Step 4 now uses the RZ node's description of points and its open injection. The two new nodes were removed from the item's stmt_deps. proof_origin was changed to agent because the Temkin PDF is missing (WANTED). Item statement unchanged.
